NextAction.description:
What the caller should do next. Closed set; agents branch on it.

A newer release can add a member, so a caller treats one it does not
recognize as its default branch.

oneOf.description: No app carries client credentials; register one.
The target app has credentials and no token; sign in.
Another app is the one to use; rerun naming it.
The store could not be read or parsed; look at the file.
X refused the app; enroll it in the developer portal.

The invocation was not one the tool takes, a word that names no
command or a usage error; read the help it names.

Media was still processing when the wait's deadline passed; wait on
the same media id again.

X rate limited the request and said when the window resets; send it
again once that time has passed.
Nothing is wrong with the request; send it again.

The input, or the local state the command read, is what failed, and
no other command repairs it; change it before another try.
The tool or the library is at fault; report it.

The command destroys something and ran without its confirmation;
run it again with the flag that confirms it.
One other command repairs this; run it.

NextStep.description:
The `next_step` object carried by an error envelope.

At most one of [`Self::command`] and [`Self::template`] is present: a
command is a verbatim invocation safe for a non-TTY caller, while a
template is one the caller finishes or decides on before running it. It
carries angle-bracket placeholders to fill in, or, under
[`NextAction::Confirm`], the invocation that destroys once it runs. A
step with neither names an action that is not an `xr` invocation, with
`docs` when a page covers it: [`NextAction::EnrollApp`],
[`NextAction::WaitAndRetry`], [`NextAction::Retry`],
[`NextAction::FixInput`], [`NextAction::ReportIssue`], and
[`NextAction::InspectStore`] when the command that failed is the one
that reports on the store.

command.description: A runnable invocation, when one exists.

docs.description: Documentation URL, when a recipe exists.

template.description: A placeholder invocation, when the caller must supply values.

description:
Result envelope shared by both `--output text` and `--output json`.
Uniform across success and error paths per the project envelope rules.

exit_code.description: Process exit code for the install run.

install_dir.description:
Resolved destination path, with `~` expanded or a host config- or
base-directory variable applied.

legacy_install_dir.description:
A copy of the bundle found at a location other than `install_dir` that
the host still reads, such as Codex's deprecated `~/.codex/skills`.
`skill update` removes it and installs at `install_dir`; `skill
install` leaves it in place.

next_step.description: What to do about [`Self::reason`]; `None` on success.

reason.description: Kebab-case error reason from [`InstallError::reason`]; `None` on success.

would_succeed.description: Dry-run-only: would the install have succeeded?
